args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the latest deploy, checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of about 18%. The v2.3.1 release candidate had also been unhealthy in staging. v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production, so checkout-api was rolled back to v2.3.0 in all three regions. A human approved the rollback. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before trying to redeploy it, and look into why it was promoted to production when the RC was unhealthy in staging.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions and opened a SEV2 incident. The service is healthy again.

- **Problem:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west, failing health checks with an 18% error rate.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production. A human approver signed off, and the rollback went out to all three regions. Afterwards, the service showed as healthy with a 0.2% error rate.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api) is open and the on-call engineer has been paged. It says what failed and what I did. It also lists follow-ups: find out why v2.3.1 failed, and why it reached production when its release candidate had already been unhealthy in staging.
